principles: Write ledgers only from explicit structured rows.
Keep read-only status commands free of repair side effects.
Reuse existing ProofStory ledger normalization and hash semantics.
Make malformed milestone input fail before partial ledger persistence.
drivers: The user wants automatic creation at planning write points, not implicit status repair.
Existing explicit milestone_ledger_set/add behavior must stay compatible.
Planner and plan_skeleton must not infer rows from prose or checklist text.

options.name: A: Auto set complete ledger at planning write points
pros: One atomic candidate ledger mirrors milestone_ledger_set semantics
Avoids repeated add events and duplicate row drift
cons: Callers must provide complete structured rows upfront

options.name: B: Auto add rows incrementally as planning discovers them
pros: Can append small updates over time
cons: Harder to audit as one planning intent
More duplicate handling and drift risk

options.name: C: Leave only manual milestone_ledger_set/add
cons: Does not satisfy the requested automatic planning write behavior
Leaves planner-created stories missing ledgers unless the operator remembers a separate command

chosen: A: Auto set complete ledger at planning write points
rationale: A preserves the existing explicit ledger-set contract while moving the call to legitimate planning write boundaries. It creates a candidate ledger only when structured rows are supplied and keeps read-only/status surfaces side-effect free.

preMortem.scenario: Malformed rows create a story but no ledger
preMortem.trigger: Ledger validation runs after metadata writes
preMortem.consequence: Partial story state confuses the operator
preMortem.mitigation: Build and validate the candidate ledger before story metadata persistence, then write it after the story shell exists.

preMortem.scenario: Planner starts inventing milestones from prose
preMortem.trigger: Draft prose/checklist text is used as a fallback milestone source
preMortem.mitigation: Only pass draft.milestones when it is an explicit structured array and never synthesize from text.

preMortem.scenario: Read-only plan_skeleton or milestone_status mutates files
preMortem.trigger: Convenience repair logic is shared into status/preview paths
preMortem.consequence: Preview/report commands become hidden repair commands
preMortem.mitigation: Guard writes behind explicit --write and leave milestone_status untouched.
